approved: Australian Capital Territory Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013
Sustainability, Environment, Water, Population and Communities

Moved the Australian Capital Territory Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, transferring management of water abstraction on national land in the ACT from the Commonwealth to the territory government so it can prepare a water resource plan compliant with the Murray-Darling Basin Plan made in November last year, including the Googong Dam located on New South Wales land.

Supported the ACT water management bill but criticised the pace of Murray-Darling Basin reform, saying more than 25 drafts of an intergovernmental agreement with basin states have failed to reach sign-off, and noted the government has deferred more than $100 million in water buyback spending while nearly 60 per cent of water has already been recovered without a formal strategy.

Summed up the ACT water management bill, welcoming opposition support and congratulating the minister on delivering Australia's first Murray-Darling Basin management plan, and said the bill would let the ACT government manage all water extraction within the territory, including the Googong Dam, to meet the plan's requirements.
